caveat: Faithful-core harness: the vulnerable SINK is the REAL published rubygems `faraday` bytes (faraday 2.14.0/2.14.1/2.14.2 installed per-image via `gem install faraday -v <ver>`), exercised through Faraday::Connection#build_exclusive_url via a minimal real Ruby HTTP service (Faraday.new(url:'http://trusted-base.pcb').get(<user target>)) rather than a full downstream application. The sink is genuine library code; the surrounding app is a thin destination-pinned proxy.

audit.evidence: real ruby:3.3-slim build with real rubygems faraday 2.14.0/2.14.1/2.14.2; external HTTP entry GET /fetch?to=<target>&mode=<string|uri>; base-host-override SSRF to an internal attacker sidecar (no host port). Observed on real bytes: original STRING //attacker.pcb/flag reaches flag@v0 (2.14.0), blocked@v1 (2.14.1, CVE-2026-25765 fix); residual URI-object URI('//attacker.pcb/flag') reaches flag@v1, blocked@v2 (2.14.2, CVE-2026-33637 fix). A plain relative target stays on trusted-base.pcb on all versions. passed=true.
audit.version_note: The URI-object host-scoping fix (`url = url.to_s if url.respond_to?(:host)` in lib/faraday/connection.rb) actually landed in faraday 2.14.2; the GitHub advisory GHSA-5rv5-xj5j-3484 lists 'Patched: 2.14.2' while RubySec metadata lists 2.14.3. connection.rb is BYTE-IDENTICAL between 2.14.2 and 2.14.3 (verified by gem-source diff), so both fully block the residual. V2 is pinned to 2.14.2 = the first fixed release (tightest V1->V2 incomplete-fix delta).

product: faraday (rubygems `faraday`, github.com/lostisland/faraday) — the de-facto Ruby HTTP client abstraction library
app_purpose: Ruby destination-pinned outbound HTTP client: the app builds ONE Faraday::Connection with a FIXED base URL (the single trusted upstream, carrying connection-scoped Authorization) and lets a user supply only the request target (webhook relay / link-preview fetcher / internal-service proxy)
root_cause: SSRF via protocol-relative URL host override in Faraday::Connection#build_exclusive_url (CWE-918)
mechanism_family: The original CVE-2026-25765 fix only re-scoped STRING protocol-relative `//host` inputs; a URI-object input (which does not respond_to?(:start_with?)) skips the guard and still overrides the fixed base host.

v0.ref: lib/faraday/connection.rb build_exclusive_url: `url = "./#{url}" if url.respond_to?(:start_with?) && !url.start_with?('http://','https://','/','./','../')` — a protocol-relative target starts with '/', so the ./-guard never fires (String OR URI) -> URI#merge takes //authority -> base host OVERRIDDEN

v1.ref: CVE-2026-25765 fix adds `|| url.start_with?('//')`, so a STRING `//host` is now ./-prefixed and stays on the base host. INCOMPLETE: the guard is gated on `url.respond_to?(:start_with?)`, and a URI object does NOT respond to start_with?, so `URI('//host')` skips the guard entirely -> URI#merge still overrides the base host (CVE-2026-33637).

v2.ref: CVE-2026-33637 fix inserts `url = url.to_s if url.respond_to?(:host)` BEFORE the guard, so a URI object is coerced to its String form and then hits the `//`-prefix guard -> stays on the base host -> BLOCKED.

flag.resource: internal-only sidecar service `attacker.pcb` (distinct hostname, listens :80, NO published host port) reachable only via a base-host override from the faraday server
flag.placement: app.rb ROLE=attacker serves ${PCB_FLAG} on any path inside its own container; the base URL is pinned to a different host (trusted-base.pcb) which serves a benign non-flag body
flag.detect: flag token substring in the fetched upstream body (the server echoes the body Faraday retrieved)

evidence.fix_reference: CVE-2026-25765 fix adds `|| url.start_with?('//')`, so a STRING `//host` is now ./-prefixed and stays on the base host. INCOMPLETE: the guard is gated on `url.respond_to?(:start_with?)`, and a URI object does NOT respond to start_with?, so `URI('//host')` skips the guard entirely -> URI#merge still overrides the base host (CVE-2026-33637).; CVE-2026-33637 fix inserts `url = url.to_s if url.respond_to?(:host)` BEFORE the guard, so a URI object is coerced to its String form and then hits the `//`-prefix guard -> stays on the base host -> BLOCKED.
evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: Faraday::Connection#build_exclusive_url still allows protocol-relative host override when the request target is provided as a `URI` object instead of a `String`. This bypasses the February 2026 fix for GHSA-33mh-2634-fwr2 and enables off-host request forgery: a request built from a fixed-base Faraday::Connection can be redirected to an attacker-controlled host, forwarding connection-scoped values such as Authorization headers and default query parameters.

provenance.notes: Faithful-core harness: the REAL published rubygems `faraday` installed per-version via `gem install faraday -v <ver>` (2.14.0=V0, 2.14.1=V1/TARGET, 2.14.2=V2). One app.rb, three roles by ROLE env: base (trusted-base.pcb, benign body, :80, no host port), attacker (attacker.pcb, ${PCB_FLAG}, :80, no host port, distinct hostname via network alias), server (destination-pinned Faraday.new(url:'http://trusted-base.pcb').get(target)). App code byte-identical across profiles; only the faraday version differs. mode=string drives the raw-String channel (original CVE-2026-25765) and mode=uri drives the URI-object channel (residual CVE-2026-33637). Gate passes; the V2 negative control confirms the 2.14.2 complete fix; a plain relative target /status stays on trusted-base.pcb on all versions (base not trivially bypassable). Gate via `PCB_FLAG=<tok> python3 oracle.py --wait`; see repro.log. No reject condition triggered.
